description:
FILED s451 (Fable, round-10 early-sweep attribution).  PRE-EXISTING measurement artifact, exposed as 2 LOST rows by #542.

MECHANISM (probed on 718db6b AND on the X+W+Y tree, reset.t + tr.t, manual child A/B): during p-load-with-recovery eval, an SBCL stderr diagnostic ("While evaluating the form starting at line N, column 0\n  of #P\"...\":") is written in MULTIPLE writes and its line is left UNTERMINATED mid-way; the next stdout write lands mid-line in the merged capture (the sweep runs >$tmp 2>&1), so exactly ONE TAP row loses its column-0 anchor and the parser cannot count it.  This glued on BOTH trees all along -- the baseline counts already include one glued-away row per affected file.  #542 (stdout :full to a file) only moved WHICH row lands at the glue point: base glued a "# skip" row (not in the pass count), main glues a real pass (reset.t ok 35 "no crash if package is effectively renamed before op is freed"; tr.t ok 223 "RT #36622 y/// at end of file") -- hence reset.t 41->40 and tr.t 239->238, serially stable, ruled interleave family (pass-baseline edited by hand with this task as cause, s451).

CONSEQUENCE UNTIL FIXED: any change that shifts output volume moves the glue point, producing recurring +/-1 pass-baseline churn in PARTIAL files with stderr diagnostics.

FIX SHAPE (harness-only, no perl-fidelity constraint -- the diagnostic is SBCL/PCL-side, perl never prints it): in cl/pcl-test.lisp p-load-with-recovery, bind *error-output* around the (eval form) to a line-atomic wrapper over the real stderr (accumulate until #\Newline, then ONE write-string + finish; flush the remainder terminated at form end) -- glue becomes impossible regardless of who writes unterminated pieces, and stdout blocks can only land BETWEEN whole stderr lines.  Identify the actual writer while there ("While evaluating the form starting at line" -- SBCL eval/compile context printer; note whether the message tail is genuinely never written or lands elsewhere).  NOTE the two glued rows RESURFACE when fixed: expect reset.t 40->41-ish and tr.t 238->239-ish (the glued row returns; re-verify identities, the skip-vs-pass mix decides exact counts) -- pass-baseline edited back by hand with this task as cause.

BAR: the reset.t + tr.t manual child A/B (the s451 recipe: replicate the sweep child command, grep for mid-line "ok N"); zero glued rows in both; full sweep with the two pass-baseline rows edited back; no new interleave movers.

DONE s452aa (Opus agent AA, round 11).

THE WRITER, IDENTIFIED (the task asked): SBCL's own context note

    While evaluating the form starting at line 149, column 0
      of #P"/home/bernt/.pcl-cache/3C3F67C268D51FD9.lisp":

printed by a HANDLER-BIND on ERROR inside sb-impl::load-as-source.  Two
consequences the task guessed at and that are now measured:
  * it is reached because an eval'd form LOADs a CACHED MODULE TRANSPILE from
    ~/.pcl-cache -- that inner `load` is the load-as-source with the handler;
  * because it is handler-BIND, it prints as the condition goes PAST, and a
    perl-level `eval {}` then handles the error, so nothing else is ever
    printed.  That is why the message tail looked missing: there is no tail.
    Its own trailing ~% is simply a SEPARATE write from the text, and that
    inter-write gap is where the stdout slab landed.

FIX (cl/pcl-test.lisp, harness-only): p-load-with-recovery binds *error-output*
for the WHOLE load to %line-atomic-stream, a Gray output stream that buffers
until a newline and then emits the line in ONE write-string + finish-output;
%las-flush-terminated runs after every top-level form and in an unwind-protect
at the end, so nothing unterminated can survive a form boundary or an `exit`.
stream-force-output / stream-finish-output deliberately do NOT flush a partial
line -- that is the one thing the stream exists to prevent.  The binding spans
the recovery diagnostics too, so those cannot glue either.  stream-write-string
takes a BULK path (split at the last newline) because this stream sees every
warning a suite file prints.

WHY THE BINDING IS SAFE (both hazards checked, not assumed):
  * fileno(STDERR) does NOT go through *error-output*: %p-fileno-impl asks
    %p-fd-of-stream FIRST and the *p-filehandles* STDERR entry is the real
    fd-stream, so the `(eq stream *error-output*)` fallback is never reached
    for it.
  * `open STDERR, '>', â¦` inside the file setf's the binding, and because the
    binding spans the WHOLE load (not each form), every later form sees the new
    stream, exactly as before.  What is still pending in the wrapper is flushed
    to the ORIGINAL stderr at the end.

A/B BY THE s451 RECIPE (replicate the sweep child command, grep for a mid-line
"ok N"), old harness vs new on the same tree:
    reset.t   glued 1 -> 0    anchored TAP rows 44 -> 45
              returning row = `ok 35 - no crash if package is effectively
              renamed before op is freed`   (exactly as predicted)
    tr.t      glued 1 -> 0    anchored TAP rows 314 -> 315
              returning row = `ok 223 - RT #36622 y/// at end of file`
EXPECTED SWEEP MOVEMENT: reset.t 40 -> 41 and tr.t 238 -> 239 passing; both rows
go back into baselines/pass-baseline.tsv by EDIT with this task as the cause.

re/charset.t does NOT move: measured on the fixed tree at C 2776/2775, which is
its blessed snapshot row exactly, with ZERO glued rows in the kept output.  The
round-10 C_notok 2776 -> 2775 there has a different cause and stays spliced.
